name: comp-319

frames.best_why: Frame 5 shows the bottom of the terms with I agree finally enabled.

tagline: Terms dialog keeps I agree disabled until you scroll to the end.
summary: A trigger opens a narrow dialog of legal text. An outlined Cancel sits beside a dimmed I agree that only lights up once the body is scrolled to the bottom.
appearance: Closed, a single outlined button. Open, a tall dark rounded dialog: a bordered title bar reading Terms & Conditions, dense small legal paragraphs with bold clause names, and a bordered footer with a grey hint plus Cancel and I agree.
behaviour: Scrolling the body toward the bottom flips I agree from dim and disabled to an active button, and the footer hint disappears. Cancel or Escape closes the dialog.
demo_content: Legal text on acceptance of terms, account responsibilities, content use, liability, conduct, changes and termination.
search_phrases: legal terms scroll box with cancel
use_when: You must record explicit acceptance of long terms and want to push readers to the end.
avoid_when: The gate only checks scroll position, so it can be bypassed and proves nothing was read.
customise: Every clause, heading and label is hardcoded; the only logic is a scroll check and an enabled flag.
weight_why: One dialog with a scroll listener; no animation beyond the opening fade.

a11y.note: The dialog traps focus and Escape closes it, but nothing announces that I agree has unlocked after scrolling.

issues: The read gate only checks scroll position, so it does not verify anything was read.
Dense legal copy in a narrow column is slow to scan.
polish_why: The unlock pattern reads clearly, but the wall of legal filler looks generic.
